title: Dual and plural: pronouns and suffixes

blocks.text: So far you've spoken of "Io" , "Tu" , "Lui" , "Lei" . Arabic has eight other pronouns: in addition to the plural it has the dual, a form specifically for two "voi" and "their" two "s," and distinguishes the male from the female also to the plural. In this unit complete the table of independent pronouns and suffixes, learn to form the dual names and talk about groups: your team, your office, your class. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 30–31 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-12), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use all thirteen independent pronouns, including dual and female plural;
2. attack all suffixes to names and prepositions ( ⁧كِتَابُنَا، مَعَهُمْ، عِنْدَكُمْ⁩ );
3. apply the -hum → -him step and -humā → -himā;
4. form the dual of names ( ⁧طَالِبَانِ⁩ / ⁧طَالِبَيْنِ⁩ );
5. build nominal phrases with plural subject using the plurals you know as vocabulary;
6. present your team or office in 60 words.

What to notice. Salmā use ⁧أَنْتُمَا⁩ You two with the couples and ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ You are with the whole class. The dual can also be seen in the names: ⁧طَالِبَانِ⁩ • two students: ⁧صَدِيقَتَانِ⁩ Two friends. ⁧كُتُبُنَا⁩ • our books • • ⁧كُتُبُكُمْ⁩ Your books are: the plural suffixes. In ⁧أَنْتُمُ الآنَ⁩ the m takes a support u in front of the alif waṣla, as in ⁧عَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ⁩ .
3a female ⁧هِيَ⁩ Hiya her ⁧هُمَا⁩ humā The two of them ⁧هُنَّ⁩ Hunna their (women)
The way they're used.
• Mixed groups: male plural ( ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ , ⁧هُمْ⁩ ). One man in the group is enough.
• Women only: ⁧أَنْتُنَّ⁩ , ⁧هُنَّ⁩ . Many people in the talk use masculine also for female groups; in the texts written on Female is regular.
• Two people: the dual ⁧أَنْتُمَا⁩ , ⁧هُمَا⁩ , same for male and female. In the speech it often replaces with the plural; in the texts and in the news the dual is systematic.
• ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ It applies to men and women, to two or more people.

Plural of respect. In some official letters and formal speeches (Golfo, protocol) ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ It is used for one rank person only, and the sovereigns speak of themselves with ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ . Recognize it. It's not a mistake.
It forms by adding -āni (name case) or -ayni (parent and accusative) to the singular. The ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ .

The dual is enough for itself. ⁧طَالِبَانِ⁩ It already means two students: ⁧اثْنَانِ⁩ is added only to insist. The adjective agrees with the dual: ⁧طَالِبَانِ جَدِيدَانِ⁩ , ⁧فِي سَيَّارَتَيْنِ صَغِيرَتَيْنِ⁩ . After preposition the dual goes to the genitive: ⁧مَعَ طَالِبَيْنِ⁩ With two students. In pause the final -i falls: ṭālibān , ṭālibayn . To be recognized. In front of a suffix or a second termiḍāfa the ⁧ن⁩ falls: ⁧كِتَابَا الطَّالِبِ⁩ The two books of the student are: ⁧يَدَاهُ⁩ His two hands are in. I will look into it in A2.
With a plural subject (people) the predicate goes to the plural. The plural names you already know as a vocabulary; the rules for training them are in A1-15.

Two models. Many adjectives and professional names and the nisba make plural with -ūna (male) and -āt (female): ⁧مُهَنْدِسُونَ⁩ , ⁧مِصْرِيُّونَ⁩ , ⁧مَشْغُولُونَ⁩ , ⁧مُهَنْدِسَاتٌ⁩ . Others have an inside plural to learn: ⁧طُلَّاب⁩ , ⁧زُمَلَاء⁩ , ⁧أَصْدِقَاء⁩ , ⁧رِجَال⁩ . It is the subject of A1-15.

⁧السَّلَامُ⁩ .

The hamza in front of the suffixes. In the -āʾ the hamza changes support according to the appropriate vowel (L0-09): ⁧زُمَلَاؤُنَا⁩ (name) ⁧مَعَ زُمَلَائِنَا⁩ (genitive). Reading doesn't change anything: it's always ʾ .
Now you understand in full ⁧السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ⁩ Peace on you and ⁧أَهْلًا بِكُمْ⁩ Welcome.

⁧ح⁩ in ⁧نَحْنُ⁩ . naḥnu : ḥāʾ Faringale, not h. nahnu is a frequent mistake. The šadda of ⁧أَنْتُنَّ⁩ and ⁧هُنَّ⁩ . antunna , hunna: the double n is the only sign that distinguishes them when listening from ⁧أَنْتُمْ⁩ / ⁧هُمْ⁩ (in addition to m). The dual on pause. ṭālibān , ṣadīqatān : ā is long and the end n feels. In front of an adjective: ṭālibāni ǧadīdān . -kumā and -humā. Accento on the penultimate: kitābuKUmā , baytiHImā .

Notes of use. ⁧نَاس⁩ is a collective that agrees to the plural: ⁧النَّاسُ هُنَا كَثِيرُونَ⁩ There are a lot of people here. ⁧كُلّ⁩ followed by an indeterminate name means "every" ( ⁧كُلُّ طَالِبٍ⁩ • each student •), followed by a specific name or suffix •all of them ( ⁧كُلُّ الطُّلَّابِ⁩ , ⁧كُلُّهُمْ⁩ All of them. ⁧مَوْجُود⁩ is the word by which you answer the appeal and say "there is / there is no" for people: ⁧المُدِيرُ مَوْجُودٌ؟⁩ Is the director here?
